Fed minutes lean hawkish but the week's pullback in high-quality tech themes with strong prior trends (cybersecurity, defense) looks like temporary de-risking rather than fundamental deterioration, and geopolitical tension (Iran, Brent $92.67) supports defense demand.

Crypto continuations are too extended and low quality to trust for another week.
key_risks: NVIDIA earnings Aug 26 could swing all tech-adjacent themes sharply either way; Hawkish Fed tone and a 5.27% 30-year yield could pressure high-beta growth further; A geopolitical de-escalation would remove the defense-sector tailwind; Crypto momentum could persist another week, making momentum-fade ranks costly

rationale_summary: SPY fell 1.4% on the week with breadth rotating away from mega-cap tech toward defensives, healthcare, precious metals and international. Rates remain elevated (10y 4.74%, 30y 5.27%) with hawkish FOMC minutes, so long-duration growth is under pressure. NVIDIA earnings on August 26 is the dominant single-name catalyst inside the scoring window and cuts both ways for semis and AI baskets. Cross-sectional dispersion is high (5.2% 5-session active spread) and crypto has spiked on huge volume, which is stretched rather than a fresh edge. Best risk-adjusted reversal candidates are high-quality tech-adjacent groups with strong prior relative trend and a sharp one-week pullback: cybersecurity, aerospace/defense, and to a lesser degree autonomous robotics.
portfolio_rationale: Only two candidates clear the overreaction plus 55% bar: CIBR and ITA, both high-quality groups with strong prior relative trends and unusually deep one-week relative pullbacks unexplained by briefing fundamentals. ARKQ ranks third on quality but its NVIDIA-earnings beta and lack of a clean overreaction signature keep it below the eligibility threshold, leaving the remaining slot in SPY. Crypto's parabolic three-session move and solar's persistent deterioration are avoided.
key_risks: NVIDIA's Aug 26 results could trigger a broad tech/AI drawdown that hits cybersecurity and robotics alongside semis; Hawkish rate repricing with 10y at 4.74% and 30y at 5.27% pressures high-beta growth baskets; Aerospace/defense weakness may reflect unreported order or budget news rather than a temporary overreaction; High cross-sectional dispersion (5.2%) means one-week sector outcomes are wide and noisy; A sharp crypto or commodity unwind could spill into broader risk appetite before the Aug 31 close

rationale_summary: SPY soft on the week amid sticky inflation prints, softer labor revisions, elevated long rates, and geopolitics supporting oil; Friday bounce and strong PMI contrast with crypto/precious-metal surges and selective equity pullbacks, yielding mixed continuation versus shock-reversal setups into NVDA and data releases.
portfolio_rationale: Highest-conviction edges are moderate mean-reversion in high-quality or low-beta names that sold off hard without clear fundamental breaks; aerospace leads on geopolitics plus deepest slate shock, cybersecurity on top quality pullback scores, and regional banks on low beta oversold tape. Extended crypto and low-quality solar lack reliable one-week excess edge; semis carry NVDA binary risk without clear overreaction label strength. Prefer SPY as baseline given only thin probabilistic edges.
key_risks: NVIDIA results and July PCE/GDP revisions mid-window can reverse tech and beta factors sharply; Further Middle East / tanker escalation could spike oil and risk-off equities beyond defense bounce; Elevated long-end yields and hawkish Fed minutes residual may pressure duration-sensitive and high-vol growth names; Crypto and metals momentum unwind could lift cross-asset vol and correlation to SPY
